What was the loudest sound in human history?
A volcano called Krakatoa, in Indonesia, exploded.
A British ship was about forty miles away.
Its captain wrote that the eardrums of over half his crew were shattered.
That's not even the crazy part.
On an island near Mauritius, almost three thousand miles away, people heard it...
and thought it was distant cannon fire.
And the pressure wave kept going.
Barometers all over the world caught it circling the planet...
again and again, for five days.
So the whole Earth felt it?
Giant waves killed more than thirty-six thousand people.
Then the ash spread across the sky...
and sunsets around the world turned blood red.
In New York state, people saw the sky glowing and called the fire department...
because they thought a town was burning.
and the whole planet heard it.
